name: Sámi sky
summary: The sky of the indigenous people of northern Scandinavia: the great elk Sarva and the archers hunting it.

001.name: Sarva, the Elk
001.description: The ruling figure of the sky: a huge elk made of Cassiopeia, Perseus and part of Auriga. The stars around it are all figures hunting it. It probably dates from a hunting culture that predates the domestication of the reindeer.

002.name: Favdna’s Bow and Arrow
002.description: The stars of the Plough: the hunter’s bow, with which he takes aim at the elk.

003.name: Galla’s Sons
003.description: The three stars of Orion’s Belt, Galla’s sons, the hunter’s helpers.

004.name: The Pillar of the Sky
004.description: The Pole Star holds up the sky. According to the legend, if Favdna’s arrow hits it, the world will end.

005.name: Favdna, the Hunter
005.description: Arcturus: the hunter who takes aim at the elk with his bow.

006.name: The Runner
006.description: Vega, one of the hunt’s helpers.

007.name: The Morning Star
007.description: The star that announces the approach of morning on Johan Turi’s sky map. It may also be Venus; here it is linked to Altair.

008.name: The Pack of Dogs
008.description: The Pleiades: a pack of hunting dogs. Another name is the “calf herd” (Miese-cora).

009.name: Galla
009.description: Procyon, one of the hunter’s helpers. The identification is uncertain: it could also be Rigel or Sirius, but the latter is barely visible in the northern lands inhabited by the Sámi.

010.name: The Skiers
010.description: The two bright stars of Gemini, Castor and Pollux: two skiing hunters.
